### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db2315c5e70ee18c6dd6cabde6f97f933e9ad2a8` — the merge of head `825365af7b6ef38c61ed77e653558a8b09b09d7d` into base `614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db2315c5e70ee18c6dd6cabde6f97f933e9ad2a8 && git checkout db2315c5e70ee18c6dd6cabde6f97f933e9ad2a8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45 825365af7b6ef38c61ed77e653558a8b09b09d7d && git checkout -B drift-repro 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45 && git merge --no-ff 825365af7b6ef38c61ed77e653558a8b09b09d7d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `825365af7b6ef38c61ed77e653558a8b09b09d7d`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23152 (body; comments `6140032316`, `6140134367`, `6140964843`, `6154722929`, `6156025157`, `6156069877`), PR #23342 (body, comments, file list), the net diff `origin/main...825365af7` (merge-base `cc14657ed`; 6 files, +298 / −1; three commits), the head's check-runs, and `origin/main` at `614fdec83` through `git show` and `git grep` only. Nothing built, run or re-run; the better-auth internals are judged through the pin that drives the real library, not read.

### ① Derived judgments

**Published surface.** Both modules are re-exported by `src/index.ts` (lines 16 and 33); `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`, tsup's entries are `src/index.ts` and `src/rate-limit-storage.ts`, and `files` is `dist` plus README and CHANGELOG, so the new test file is not surface. Over the whole net diff, exactly two exported declarations move, the two triage named:

- `AuthManager.getConsoleUrl(path: string): string` — **right.** Its body is one line over the private `getConsolePageUrl`, whose hunk is pure addition below it (the composer is byte-unchanged, and its six existing callers are untouched). The composition is canonical origin, then `uiBasePath`, then the slash-rooted `path`: the origin is `config.baseUrl` (the same value handed to better-auth as `baseURL` at `auth-manager.ts:1497`), `uiBasePath` is a config path (`packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts:557`, default `/_console`), and `path` is appended after both, so no `path` value can move the result off the deployment's own origin. The only caller in the diff passes the literal `/reset-password` from a zero-argument deps lambda; nothing caller-controlled reaches `path`. A reader with no side effects; no second URL builder.
- `IdentityImportDeps.consoleResetPasswordUrl?(): string` — **right.** Optional and additive, spelled as a method signature like the interface's other optional members (`getMetaItem?`, `getSchema?`); for a zero-argument member returning `string` the method and property spellings admit the same values.

**Behaviour of the import.**

- Member present: the reset request is `{ email, redirectTo }`; member absent: `{ email }` with no `redirectTo` key — **right**, and pinned in both directions: `toStrictEqual` on the mock's last call in `admin-import-users.test.ts`, and pin ② through a real `AuthManager` whose deps omit the member (the link still ends `?callbackURL=`). Leg D shows the absent branch cannot grow a `redirectTo` unnoticed.
- The member is invoked inside the existing per-row `try`, so a throw lands as `INVITE_EMAIL_FAILED` on a row whose account exists, the same contract as a mail failure, no rollback — **right.**
- The HTTP accept-set of `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/import-users` (request shapes, response, row codes, delivery counters) is unchanged; what changes is the emailed link's `callbackURL`. The accept-set of better-auth's `GET /reset-password/:token` is unchanged: an empty or foreign `callbackURL` is still refused. **Right.**
- The changeset's Unchanged bullet holds against the diff: the SMS invitation (`sendInviteSms`, `sendPhoneInviteSms`), the temporary-password policy and the email template are untouched.

**Security posture — right.**

- The `redirectTo` is an absolute URL on the deployment's own origin, which is the origin better-auth seeds its trusted set from: the trusted-origins block at `auth-manager.ts:2629-2695` states and measured that (1.7.1), and the pin measures it on the installed 1.7.3. The diff adds no `trustedOrigins` entry and does not touch that block.
- Pin ① runs with the origin check ON (`skipOriginCheck = false` on the resolved context; leg E reds the pin when that flip is removed): the emailed link's GET answers 302 to `https://acme.example.com/_console/reset-password?token=T`; the same token with a foreign `callbackURL` answers 403 with no `location`; `POST /reset-password` with T answers 200, so the ADR-0069 before-hooks on `/reset-password` (password policy, rate limit) still sit in the path and accept.
- Pin ① drives the plugin's real `POST /admin/import-users` mount through `registerAuthRoutes`, so the one optional wiring line is under test (leg B: deleting it reds exactly pin ①). Only the platform-admin gate's session read is a stand-in.
- Pre-existing, not a regression: with `baseUrl` unset, `getCanonicalOrigin()` falls back to `http://localhost:3000` for this link as for every other Console link the class sends.

**Docs and ADRs.** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx:988` ("a real email gets a set-your-password email") becomes true and needs no edit. No hand-written page enumerates `AuthManager`'s methods (the three Docs-Drift rows name the class only; `auth-service.mdx` mentions it for `api` and `getApi()`), so no doc row is owed. `git grep` over `docs/adr/` for `callbackURL`, `redirectTo` and `trustedOrigins` finds no decision on this surface; ADR-0069 names `/reset-password` only as a hook path, which the diff does not touch. No ADR is reversed.

**Main drift.** No commit on `origin/main` since the merge-base `cc14657ed` touches `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/`; GitHub reports the PR mergeable. The queue rebuilds on the merged generation.

**Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-13T22:07Z:** `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint · ESLint`, every `Type Check ·` and `Lint ·` row, `Check PR Size`, the claim and single-writer guards: `success`. `Test Core (1/6)`, `(2/6)`, `(5/6)`, `(6/6)`: `success`. `Test Core (3/6)` and `(4/6)`: still `in_progress` at this read, reported as such, not assumed. The full-battery rows (`Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Build Docs`) are `skipped` on a PR run by design. Green on every required context is the landing's condition, not this record's.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` **`minor`** with **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`** — **right.** The diff publishes two additive exported declarations (one public method, one optional interface member), removes or narrows nothing, and so owes no ADR-0087 marker. AGENTS.md: a `yes` takes at least `minor`; `(widening)` is the arm for an addition. The line is carried where the gates read it: PR body line 2 and the changeset body; `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- The cited precedent holds: `e148ca984` (#22463) declared an optional third argument on two exported plugin-auth bridges at `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, with a "caller that omits it keeps the earlier answer byte for byte" sentence of the same shape. The `f9ebb7dd3` (#22800) changeset's "`IdentityImportDeps` keeps its shape" closed its own type-surface category for that landing and does not bind this one, which widens the interface and says so.
- The changeset text is accurate against the diff: the Before and Now paragraphs match the card's reproduction and the pin, "both are additions; nothing existing changes shape" is verified above, and the out-of-tree-host sentence states the cost of the optional member triage chose.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations in report `6156025157`, each answered:

1. `--concurrency=2` forwarded into package scripts, so the closure build ran at pnpm's default concurrency — a note on the dev's own run, nothing in the diff; `Build Core` is green on this head. Answered.
2. Zone 2 #1 measured as ablation leg A rather than a separate probe file — the diff carries no probe file (six files, listed above) and the leg was restored with blob hashes equal to HEAD. Answered.
3. First typecheck exit 2 for the package's own missing `dist` — a prerequisite of the examples program, not a red gate; `TypeScript Type Check` is green on this head. Answered.
4. The optional member spelled as a method signature, not a property — matches the interface's existing optional members; same accepted values for this shape (judged in ①). Answered.
5. Model-free commit trailers — read on the three branch commits: `Claude-Session` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`, the pair AGENTS.md requires and the pre-push hook enforces. Answered.
6. `origin/main` not merged — measured here: no `plugin-auth` commit landed on `main` since the merge-base; the PR is mergeable; CI runs the merge ref. Answered.

`out_of_scope_findings` in report `6156025157`, each answered:

- **The invitation copy** (the import's email is the `auth.password_reset` template, whose copy tells an invitee who requested nothing to ignore it) — the seat filed it as **#23343** (open, graded by triage next, ordered after this PR). Nothing in this diff is wrong because of it: the changeset's Unchanged bullet states the copy stays, the import's own header docblock (lines 32-34) still describes "a reset-password email for rows with a real email", truthfully, and the card's secondary note now has its own carrier. One coupling for #23343 to carry, not a defect here: pin ① and pin ② select the invitation by `template === 'auth.password_reset'` (`invitationTo`), so a distinct invitation template key moves those two selectors in the same landing.
- **Carrier: none known to the run** — resolved by the filing above. Answered.

Observed within the ruling, not a flag: an out-of-tree host that builds its own deps without the member keeps today's dead link with no runtime notice — the changeset says so in words, and triage's direction chose the optional member with "a caller without the new member keeps today's link" as its pin, so a runtime warning would have been outside the direction. The only in-repo builder is wired and under the mounted pin.
